title: Odakyu Electric Railway starts an AI crossing image-analysis system at four Odawara Line crossings that signals approaching trains to stop when people are left inside
summary: ITmedia (22 Jun 2026): from 24 Jun 2026 AI analyzes existing crossing cameras, tracks pedestrians, wheelchair users, cyclists and motorcyclists and sends a brake signal to approaching trains; devel...
account: ITmedia's 岡田有花 reported on 22 Jun 2026 that Odakyu Electric Railway announced the introduction, from 24 June 2026, of an 'AI踏切画像解析システム' at four crossings on its Odawara Line: Minami-Shinjuku Nos. 2, 4 and 5 between Minami-Shinjuku and Sangubashi stations and Mukogaoka-Yuen No. 9 between Mukogaoka-Yuen and Ikuta stations. The AI analyzes footage from the existing safety-confirmation cameras in real time, identifies and tracks pedestrians, wheelchair users, bicycles and motorcycles, and when it detects someone left inside after the barriers come down it sends a signal through the signaling equipment that applies the brakes of approaching trains and lights the crossing's special signal lamps to alert crews; both are released automatically once the crossing is clear. Images are used only for hazard detection, not to identify individuals, and analysis data are destroyed within a year. The system was developed by Meitetsu EI Engineer, Toyota Systems and Toho Electric Industries and trialled from January 2023, with work on detection accuracy at night and in rain. railf.jp carried the same announcement on 25 Jun 2026. No detection events or outcomes are reported; the date given is the operational start date.
purpose: The system is built to detect people left inside a closed crossing and stop approaching trains automatically.
system: AI踏切画像解析システム (AI crossing image-analysis system) using existing crossing cameras linked to signaling equipment
developer: Meitetsu EI Engineer, Toyota Systems and Toho Electric Industries
taxonomy_note: No type covers crossing safety; chosen because the system automates a safety check previously dependent on drivers and crossing equipment. Launch report based on the operator's announcement; the previous verifier noted Odakyu material as vendor-authored, and here two Japanese news reports and the OECD AIM entry are the fetched sources. No detection or stop event is documented.
